description: A structured search query against a Synapse SearchIndex, composed of a main full-text query, zero or more structured filters, optional facet aggregations, and response-shaping options (sort, highlight, pagination). Most callers will set at least queryText (or leave it empty for a catalog-style MATCH_ALL browse) and possibly queryType + queryFields. For advanced compound queries (e.g. mixing semantic and lexical clauses with dis_max) supply the opaque 'query' object instead — it takes precedence over queryType/queryText/queryFields. Filters, facets, sort, and returnFields are independent layers — any combination is valid. Filters run in non-scoring context: they narrow the result set without influencing relevance.

query.description:
Optional. An OpenSearch query-DSL object — the contents of the query key only (NOT the whole search request, and NOT wrapped in an outer {"query": ...} envelope). When present, this takes precedence over queryType / queryText / queryFields; the server uses it as the scoring query and still AND-s the structured filters (termsFilters, rangeFilters, exists/notExists) into filter context around it. The index, pagination, facets, sort, highlight, and source-field selection remain server-controlled — only the scoring query is caller-supplied.

Field references use column names, not internal ids — every column is exposed as an OpenSearch field alias of its name, so {"match": {"abstract": "amyloid"}} works directly. A match against a semantic-enriched column is rewritten to a neural sparse query by AOSS; a multi_match is not (so combine per-column match clauses under dis_max or bool.should for a mixed semantic + lexical search).

Allowlisted clause types only. Permitted: match, multi_match, match_phrase, match_phrase_prefix, match_bool_prefix, term, terms (inline values only — the cross-index lookup form is rejected), range, exists, prefix, wildcard, fuzzy, ids, simple_query_string, match_all, and the compound clauses bool, dis_max, constant_score, boosting. Any other clause type (e.g. script, script_score, function_score, more_like_this, geo_shape indexed lookup, has_child/has_parent, percolate, wrapper) is rejected with HTTP 400, as is a subtree deeper than 20 levels or wider than 256 clauses. This keeps the query benign (no scripting) and confined to the single SearchIndex being queried (no cross-collection reach).

Example — universal search bar over a semantic-enriched abstract plus a lexical title:

"query": {
  "dis_max": {
    "tie_breaker": 0.3,
    "queries": [
      { "match": { "abstract": "beach sandals" } },
      { "multi_match": { "query": "beach sandals", "fields": ["title^3", "keywords"] } }
    ]
  }
}

queryType.description: The full-text query model applied to queryText. Default: SIMPLE_QUERY_STRING (safe for untrusted user input). See SearchQueryType for a per-value explanation of scoring model, accepted parameters, and when to use each. When queryText is null or empty, queryType is automatically coerced to MATCH_ALL regardless of this setting.

queryText.description: The text to search for. Interpretation depends on queryType: SIMPLE_QUERY_STRING parses operators like +, -, |, "...", ~, *, (); MATCH / MULTI_MATCH analyze it into tokens and run each against the indexed tokens; MATCH_PHRASE treats it as an ordered phrase; PREFIX treats the final token as a prefix; WILDCARD treats * and ? as glob wildcards. Null or empty triggers MATCH_ALL.

queryFields.description: Columns to search, with optional per-field boost using 'field^N' syntax (e.g. 'title^3' weighs title matches three times as much as unboosted fields). Empty or null means all indexed fields. Required for MATCH, MATCH_PHRASE, and WILDCARD (single field); optional for MULTI_MATCH and PREFIX (multi-field); ignored by SIMPLE_QUERY_STRING when empty (searches every indexed field).

termsFilters.description: Multi-value IN-clause filters. Each entry restricts a column to a specified set of values; set 'not: true' on an entry to express NOT IN. Runs in non-scoring context against the column's keyword sub-field, so filter values must match stored tokens exactly (case-sensitive for text columns analyzed with lowercase filters — compare your values to what the analyzer produced).

rangeFilters.description: Inclusive range filters on numeric or date columns. Each entry restricts a column to min <= value <= max; either bound may be omitted for open-ended ranges. Values are strings and are parsed per the column type (integer, double, date). Runs in non-scoring context.

existsFilters.description: Column names that must have a non-null value in the matched documents. Useful for narrowing to rows that have been fully annotated. Runs in non-scoring context.

notExistsFilters.description: Column names that must be null or missing in the matched documents. Inverse of existsFilters; useful for surfacing under-annotated rows. Runs in non-scoring context.

fuzziness.description: Typo tolerance expressed as a Levenshtein edit distance. Accepted values: 'AUTO' (recommended — 0 edits for tokens <=2 chars, 1 edit for 3-5 chars, 2 edits for >=6 chars), '0' (disabled, exact), '1', '2'. Only meaningful for queryType=MATCH or MULTI_MATCH — OpenSearch silently ignores fuzziness on other query types. See SearchQueryType for the right alternative per type (e.g. per-term '~' syntax in queryText for SIMPLE_QUERY_STRING, or an edge-ngram analyzer for PREFIX autocomplete).

facetRequests.description: Columns to aggregate as facet buckets alongside the primary hit results. Each entry produces one terms aggregation; use maxValueCount to cap the bucket count, and sortField/sortDirection to order buckets by count or by key. Returned in SearchQueryResults.facets only when the caller opts into the FACETS response part. For aggregations beyond a terms facet (histograms, stats, cardinality, ranges, nested sub-aggregations), supply the opaque 'aggregations' object instead — it takes precedence over facetRequests.

aggregations.description:
Optional. An OpenSearch aggregations object — the contents of the aggs / aggregations key (a map of aggregation name to aggregation definition), NOT wrapped in an outer envelope. When present it takes precedence over facetRequests; the raw aggregation results are returned as a JSON string in SearchQueryResults.aggregationResults when the FACETS response part is requested (and facets is left empty).

Field references use column names (resolved by the per-column field aliases), and which columns are aggregatable follows from the Synapse column type — keyword / numeric / date / boolean columns carry doc values; analyzed text columns do not.

Allowlisted aggregation types only. Permitted: terms, histogram, date_histogram, range, date_range, min, max, avg, sum, stats, extended_stats, value_count, cardinality, missing, plus nested sub-aggregations via aggs / aggregations. Script-based aggregations (e.g. scripted_metric), pipeline aggregations, and any embedded script are rejected with HTTP 400, as is a tree deeper than 10 levels or wider than 100 aggregations.

Example — publications per year plus the citation-count distribution:

"aggregations": {
  "per_year": { "date_histogram": { "field": "published_on", "calendar_interval": "year" } },
  "citation_stats": { "stats": { "field": "citation_count" } }
}

returnFields.description: Columns to include in each hit's field list. Empty or null returns every indexed column on the matched documents. Narrowing this to the columns the caller actually displays reduces response size and transport cost, especially for wide SearchIndexes.

sort.description: Result ordering. Each entry specifies a column name (or the special '_score' pseudo-column, which sorts by relevance) and an ASC/DESC direction. When omitted, results are sorted by relevance descending (_score DESC). Sort columns must be stored as keyword or numeric sub-fields — for text columns this is handled automatically by routing through the keyword sub-field.

highlight.description: When true, each hit's field list includes HTML-tagged excerpts showing where the query matched. Uses OpenSearch's default highlighter with <em> tags around matched terms. Default: false. Ignored by autocomplete endpoint. For control over which columns, snippet size, snippet count, or tags, set 'highlightOptions' instead (which implies highlighting even when this flag is false).

highlightOptions.description: Optional. Fine-grained highlighting controls (fields, fragment size/count, tags). When present, highlighting is applied regardless of the boolean 'highlight' flag.

suggest.description:
Optional. An OpenSearch suggesters object — the contents of the suggest key (a map of suggestion name to suggester definition, optionally with a top-level text). Returns query-assistance suggestions (did-you-mean / completion) as a JSON string in SearchQueryResults.suggestResults.

Field references use column names (resolved by the per-column aliases). Allowlisted suggester types only: term, phrase, completion. Any other suggester, and any embedded script (e.g. a phrase collate script), is rejected with HTTP 400.

Example — did-you-mean over the title column:

"suggest": {
  "did_you_mean": { "text": "amiloid", "term": { "field": "title" } }
}

offset.description: Zero-based pagination offset into the hit list. Default: 0. For deep pagination (offset > ~10,000), prefer reshaping the query with filters and sort to narrow the result set rather than scrolling.

limit.description: Maximum number of hits to return per page. Default: 25. Maximum: 100 (larger values are silently capped). Set to 0 in combination with FACETS-only response parts to retrieve only aggregate counts.

collapse.description: Optional. The name of a column to collapse (deduplicate) results on — only the single top-scoring hit per distinct value of this column is returned (e.g. one row per study). The column must be a keyword / numeric / date / boolean type that carries doc values; collapsing on an analyzed text column is rejected by OpenSearch. Applied only when hits are requested. totalHits still reflects the pre-collapse match count.

searchAfter.description: Optional. Cursor for deep, stable pagination past the offset window (OpenSearch caps offset+limit at ~10,000). To page forward, echo the nextSearchAfter value from the previous response verbatim — it is an opaque token; do not construct or parse it. When set, offset is ignored (the cursor defines the position) and the server appends a row-id tiebreaker to your sort so the ordering is total and deterministic. Omit on the first page; a null nextSearchAfter in the response means there are no more pages.
